test_title: PYST 27: SSC GD Constable - Quantitative Aptitude (Held on: 25th November 2021 Shift 1)
subject: maths
question: 23 oranges were bought for Rs. 193.20 and sold at the rate of Rs. 108 per dozen. Find the profit percentage correct to one decimal place.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Find the cost and selling price for a single orange to make the calculation simple and direct.

Cost Price (CP) of 1 orange = 193.20 ÷ 23 = ₹8.40

Selling Price (SP) of 1 orange = 108 ÷ 12 = ₹9.00

Profit % = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100 = (0.60 ÷ 8.40) × 100

Profit % = (1 ÷ 14) × 100 = 7.14% ≈ 7.1%

**∴ The correct answer is 7.1%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

CP of 23 oranges = ₹193.20

SP of 1 dozen (12 oranges) = ₹108

**Formula Used:**

Profit = Selling Price (SP) − Cost Price (CP)

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f5608d2799a4f04ef69a8cd20124641f3b7aec78a279ae33eeba93ce1ef2d4cf.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ CP of 1 orange = 193.20 ÷ 23 = ₹8.40

⇒ SP of 1 orange = 108 ÷ 12 = ₹9.00

⇒ Profit earned on 1 orange = 9.00 − 8.40 = ₹0.60

⇒ Profit % = (0.60 ÷ 8.40) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (6 ÷ 84) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (1 ÷ 14) × 100

⇒ Profit % = 50 ÷ 7 = 7.1428%

⇒ Correct to one decimal place = 7.1%

**∴ The correct answer is 7.1%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). The resulting price is Selling Price (SP) = MP − Discount.

Successive Discounts

If successive discounts of x% and y% are given on an item, the equivalent single discount is given by the formula (x + y − xy÷100)%.

Dishonest Dealer Formula

If a dealer claims to sell goods at Cost Price but uses false weights, Profit % = [(True Weight − False Weight) ÷ False Weight] × 100.
